clue.text: Managing fix in company Golf

indicators.note: the word fix is placed inside the letters for company and Golf

parts.note: G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to fix something to a board is to pin it

explanation.surface: Someone getting by while patching things up at a golf firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Coping means getting by or handling a situation, as does managing.

clue.text: Sound of one with cold chest

indicators.note: the phrase tells us to say the description of a cold sufferer out loud

parts.note: someone with a cold is a person who coughs, a cougher

explanation.surface: A sick person's congested chest makes a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' looks like part of the cold sufferer's body, but it is the definition: a strongbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strongbox, a chest for storing money or valuables.

clue.text: Army unit inordinately entertained by strategy

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: a strategy is a plan
inordinately means excessively, too much

explanation.surface: A body of troops lavishly hosted as part of a military scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a subdivision of a company of soldiers, a small military unit.

clue.text: Enthusiasts stagger when going uphill

indicators.note: in a down clue, going uphill means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to stagger someone is to stun them

explanation.surface: Keen hikers totter as they climb a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is informal for fans or devotees, as in golf nuts.

clue.text: Native American secretary retiring before long

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the second in the answer
something retiring draws back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: An Indigenous American assistant is soon to retire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a group of Indigenous peoples of the American Southwest.

clue.text: Chief dislikes bagpipe that escort bears

indicators.note: the phrase carries the answer within its letters, as one bears a load

explanation.surface: A piper's escort puts up with the bagpipes, his chief annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' points to letters held in the run bagpiPE THAT EScort.
explanation.definitionFit: Pet hates are things one especially dislikes, one's main peeves.

clue.text: Either side of clearing, one dog

annotationWithheld.why: Either side of clearing, one dog (5): CORGI reads 'Either side of clearing' as 'C or G' (OR between the first and last letters of clearing) + I; 'Either' gives OR and also places it between the sides, so no separate word signals the insertion
annotationWithheld.clue: Either side of clearing, one dog

clue.text: Appear regularly in tea garden meet up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
every other letter of the phrase is taken at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Show up on time for a meeting in the tea garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'tea garden meet', EGREME, and 'up' turns that string round.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come into view, to appear.

clue.text: French worker in charge, overwrought

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A French employee who is the boss is stressed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic means wild with worry or excitement, emotionally overwrought.

clue.text: Partner several miles below mountain pass

indicators.note: in a down clue, the second piece sits under the first

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountain peaks
a league is an old measure of distance, about three miles

explanation.surface: A companion trekking many miles beneath an alpine pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is a fellow worker, a partner or associate in a job.

clue.text: Scripture lesson penned by the cardinal

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed by it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: A religious reading written out by a senior Catholic churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' looks like the churchman of the surface, but it means a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are the counting numbers, and three is one of them.

clue.text: London landmark painful to go around

indicators.note: going around here means turning back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: something painful is sore

explanation.surface: A London sight that hurts to walk round.
explanation.definitionFit: The statue known as Eros stands at Piccadilly Circus in London, a famous landmark.

clue.text: In stew, tangible evidence of lamb?

indicators.note: a stew mixes its ingredients up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Meat in a casserole is solid proof that lamb was used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' suggests a lamb stew, but it signals the anagram; the lamb's evidence is the noise it makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb's baa is its cry, so this sound is a sign a lamb is near.

clue.text: Interim's "replaced" senior parliamentarian

indicators.note: the letters are put back in new places, rearranged

parts.note: the word with its S, written out as letters

explanation.surface: A stand-in cabinet member has been swapped out.
explanation.definitionFit: A government minister is a high-ranking member of parliament heading a department.

clue.text: Lionesses on the move making no sound

indicators.note: letters on the move shift around into a new order

explanation.surface: Big cats stalking prey silently.
explanation.definitionFit: Noiseless means silent, producing nothing audible.

clue.text: Broadcaster following every Bond movie

parts.note: Sky is a British TV broadcaster
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
every means all

explanation.surface: A TV channel that shows every James Bond film.
explanation.definitionFit: Skyfall is the 2012 James Bond film starring Daniel Craig.

clue.text: Spades held in reserve, few and far between

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a reserve is a spare
S is the card-game abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Spade cards kept back are scarce in a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered, scanty.

clue.text: Terribly remote rarely seen visitor

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly disordered, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An awfully distant guest who seldom drops in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visitor' suggests a houseguest; here it is a body from space briefly visiting our skies.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is an occasional caller from space, seen only fleetingly.

clue.text: Breakfast time?

definitions.meaning: oat cereal cooked in milk or water, a morning meal
British slang for a stretch in prison

explanation.definitionFit: Oats boiled in milk are a breakfast dish, and in British slang doing porridge means serving a prison sentence.

clue.text: Polish bar you are texted about

indicators.note: turned about means the letters of both pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a pub is a bar
UR is text-message shorthand for you are

explanation.surface: A message about a local bar in Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but means to shine; 'about' reverses PUBUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub up something is to buff or shine it.

clue.text: Class stay upset with odd characters being expelled

indicators.note: letters in odd positions are thrown out, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A school form stays unhappy after the oddballs are expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suggests an anagram, but it is only part of the fodder: dropping the odd letters of 'stay upset' leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a kind or category, as is a class.

clue.text: Clever leader fired by board

indicators.note: the first letter is sacked, removed from the front

parts.note: a table is a board, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A smart chief executive dismissed by the directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means capable or talented, quick-witted.

clue.text: Found amidst rubbish, old black Android

indicators.note: amidst means placed in the middle of another word

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An old black phone discovered on a rubbish dump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Android' suggests the phone system, but it is a humanoid machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is a mechanical man, which is what an android is.

clue.text: Alone at last, married couple hug

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: a brace is a pair, a couple

explanation.surface: Finally on their own, newlyweds cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace someone is to hold them in your arms, to hug.

clue.text: Skilful former forward

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
pert means cheeky, forward

explanation.surface: A talented one-time striker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' suggests a football striker, but here it means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is highly skilled, adept.

clue.text: One auctioning, say, wine collection to audience

indicators.note: the word is as heard by listeners, a homophone

parts.note: a cellar is a stock of wine

explanation.surface: An auctioneer presents a vintage wine stock to the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone putting goods under the hammer is a vendor offering them for sale.
